minutes.headline: Conservation Commission continued most hearings to Nov 15 and allowed a hazard tree cut with replanting and stump conditions.
minutes.summary: New public hearings were struck because legal ads were not placed, so they move to November 15. The commission continued several hearings, approved one tree-removal determination with replanting, tabled another, and approved an enforcement-based fix for a tree cut near a stream. Discussion also covered understaffing, a public awareness brochure, a proposed Google Drive to SharePoint move, unpaid bills and lapsed MACC membership, and volunteer invasive-species work.

what_happened.line: New public hearings were struck from the agenda because legal ads were not placed, and will be heard November 15.
The commission voted to continue the hearings for 390 Howard Street, 2011 Fire Road 16 and 143 Island Road to November 15.
The commission accepted the administrator's recommendation for a tree removal at 833 Flat Hill Road, adding a limbing condition and a saplings photo due by May 1.
The commission tabled the 70 Horizon Island Road determination to November 15 and asked for a site map of planting locations.
A tree cut at 118 Mass Ave was allowed with stump grinding, erosion controls, loam and seed, and two saplings.

why_it_matters: Anyone with a project before the Conservation Commission, such as the continued hearings, should expect it to wait until at least November 15, because the hearings were pushed back by a missed legal-ad step.
The meeting also described staffing, MUNIS access, unpaid bills and a lapsed MACC membership, which affect how quickly the commission can process permits and pay for routine work.
The 118 Mass Ave case shows that cutting a hazardous tree near a stream can require commission approval, and a speaker said the rules were not on the town website.
watch_next: The November 15 meeting, when the struck and continued hearings and the tabled 70 Horizon Island Road determination are due.
The November 20 site visit with North County Land Trust, and the chair's emails to the tax collector (brochure deadline and cost) and the town manager (SharePoint migration).
